hot.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
hot.summary: The authors test whether positive views can align separately trained text and image representations. A JEPA trained on different descriptions of the same scene learns stronger alignment than one trained on corruptions of a single description. On WIT-1024, the 109M-parameter model scores .184 against DINOv2 ViT-B, exceeding Qwen2.5-72B’s .154; the theorem’s idealized assumptions limit generalization.

hot.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
hot.summary: The authors cast pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning, and suitable reinforcement-learning updates as maximum-likelihood training with a changing data mixture. In reasoning experiments, unified schedules reach higher accuracy and coverage at larger tested compute budgets, though staged training can lead at intermediate budgets. After coding updates, a 0.76B model with 5% midtraining-data mixing scores 58.47% pass@16 versus 52.12%, limited to this continuation setup.

hot.title: Probing Spatial State Representations in Visual Foundation Models
hot.summary: The authors evaluate ten frozen visual representations for whether small probes can read visible scene structure, retain objects after they leave view, predict spatial updates under camera motion, and select goal-directed actions. VideoMAE’s out-of-view bearing error is 36.45°, versus DINOv2’s 65.38°, despite DINOv2’s stronger visible-scene readouts. These offline tests do not establish online memory or reliable robot behavior.

hot.title: Cross-Controller Transfer via In-Context Behavior Adaptation
hot.summary: The authors present a robot policy that uses behavioral context to transfer across tasks and controllers. It conditions on examples pairing commanded actions with resulting motions under the deployment controller, rather than relying only on estimated controller dynamics. In held-out task–controller cells, cross-task context reaches 50.0% success, versus 27.0% for system identification and a 75.0% same-controller upper bound. This zero-shot result uses another task’s context and comes from one robot setup.

hot.title: Training language models in simulation for psychiatric intake
hot.summary: The simulation-trained model improves psychiatric intake conversations by practicing multi-turn encounters with simulated patients and receiving rewards for clinical reasoning, communication, and safety. In a randomized, double-blind crossover study, it received higher psychiatrist transcript ratings than its identically prompted base model in 46 of 60 matched scenario pairs (76.7%). This supports improvement in controlled text encounters, not real-patient safety or effectiveness.

hot.title: Read, Allocate, Route: Role-Coupled Tokenization for Pixel-Space Generative Transformers
hot.summary: SpecSlot assigns global communication to low-frequency image carriers while keeping finer output slots local. Each anchor produces multiple slots with disjoint spectral roles, but only one joins dense global attention. On ImageNet-512 it reaches 9.14 FID versus 11.98 for a FLOPs-matched JiT-CM control, with 3.9% fewer conditional forward FLOPs; it remains 0.69 FID worse than JiT-B/16.

hot.title: L3G-World: Real-Time Infinite World Generation with Latent 3D Gaussian Memory
hot.summary: L3G-World generates interactive video worlds using a revisable 3D Gaussian scene memory that stores video-VAE features. It renders this memory into latent conditioning for each video chunk, then updates it by adding missing content and refining visible Gaussians. On DL3DV loop-closure tests, it achieves 16.00 self-consistency PSNR versus 13.96 for Spatia; Matrix-Game 3.0 has lower LPIPS, and tests use static scenes.

hot.title: Robotic Data Inoculation
hot.summary: The authors introduce DI, which keeps a human in control while an online-trained residual policy adds bounded, state-dependent changes to commands; the human can correct these deviations, creating recovery-relevant demonstrations. Across three real-world manipulation tasks, DI has the highest mean in all six task-by-method comparisons. For t-cube offline RL, success is 0.59 ± 0.02 versus 0.42 ± 0.06 with clean teleoperation; the findings do not establish general gains or safety.

hot.title: Evolving Agent Teams
hot.summary: Evolving Agent Teams changes how coding agents are organized during GPU kernel optimization. A supervisor diagnoses stalled progress, redesigns roles and coordination, and preserves lessons and code in a shared filesystem. On DeepSeek-V3 MLA paged decode, additional-budget runs achieve 1.21× geometric-mean speedup over production FlashInfer across 47 H100 workloads, with 36 faster; 11 remain slower, without beating the run-stage-only reference.

hot.title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
hot.summary: Intrinsic Distribution Matching (IDM) adds pooled feature-mean and standard-deviation matching to distribution-matching distillation while retaining its score-difference correction and short inference path. In a matched two-evaluation ablation, it raises GenEval from 77.46% to 77.81%. On Z-Image-Turbo 6B, it scores 94.25% on LongText-CN and 90.20% on LongText-EN, highest among compared methods at that budget.

hot.title: Rethinking Pre-pretraining
hot.summary: The authors test whether synthetic pre-pretraining (PPT) is a better use of a fixed training-compute budget than natural-language training. They compare synthetic-first and natural-language-only training across scarce-data, plentiful-data, and high-token regimes. Across these tested compute-matched settings, synthetic PPT does not outperform natural-language training on language modeling; this finding is limited to the tested recipes and evaluations.

hot.title: Elucidating the Design Space of LM Data Attribution
hot.summary: The authors show how token-level scoring can recover training documents that document-level attribution misses. They change the gradient loss to preserve evidence from confidently predicted answer tokens and aggregate only the highest-scoring token contributions. On CATT, this raises Recall@N by 35 to 72 percentage points across six methods. On FTRACE-TREX, negative log-odds helps, but top-10 pooling is not consistently better.

hot.title: When Requirements Interact: Scaling Long-Horizon Coding via Interdependent Specifications
hot.summary: CodeSpecWeave creates repository coding tasks in which requirements constrain one another, and builds executable tests alongside each task. Its dataset averages 8.36 specifications across 4.08 behavioral categories per task, compared with 2.15 and 1.49 for R2E-Gym. On DeepSWE-v1.1, MiMo-V2.6-Flash-SFT reports 62.98% success versus 56.64% with SWE-PI, though this comparison does not isolate coupling as the cause.

hot.title: TouchBridge: Tactile-Conditioned Human-to-Robot Transfer for Dexterous Manipulation
hot.summary: TouchBridge converts human demonstrations for contact-rich robot manipulation by recording fingertip touch alongside motion and using tactile contacts to guide transfer to a robot hand. Its retargeting aligns fingertip poses, contact patches, and relationships between fingers, without object models or simulation. Across four real-world tasks, converted data achieved 72.5% mean success versus 77.5% with teleoperation, using 60 demonstrations per task.

hot.title: Video Generation Meets Agent Harness: Agentic Video Generation, Agentic World Modeling and Recursive Self-Improvement
hot.summary: The authors survey agent harnesses as runtime layers that connect video production, interaction with video world models, and system development. They explain how harnesses select context, schedule tools, maintain state, route feedback, and enforce budgets. The framework organizes prior work and evaluation requirements, but no surveyed system shows revised development procedures improve later rounds of video-generator development.

hot.title: BURGER: Benchmarking and Understanding Robotic Generalization via Embodied Drawing
hot.summary: BURGER creates simulated robot-drawing demonstrations from language prompts, converting generated sketches into ordered strokes and recording the robot’s observations, state, and actions. Policies receive no target sketch at inference. With shared clustering, it yields 7.13 effective trajectory modes per instruction, versus 1.09 for a manipulation benchmark. This measures route diversity, not success; policies struggle with unseen object categories.

hot.title: How to Loop Your Transformer: Loop Scaling, Specialization, and Parallel Inference
hot.summary: The authors study looping, which reuses transformer weights for repeated computation, in dense decoder-only models. They compare loop designs and shifted parallel looping. In tested over-trained conditions, two-loop models at 80 tokens per parameter reach a given DCLM validation bits-per-byte with fewer training FLOPs than vanilla models at 160 tokens per parameter, without establishing general efficiency or latency gains.

hot.title: Your LR Schedule May Not Be Principled: Effective Learning Rate Scheduling in Weight-Normalized Training
hot.summary: The authors show that effective learning rate—nominal learning rate divided by parameter-block norm—helps explain differences between weight normalization and weight decay. Matching interventions align loss dynamics, while AIR adjusts inverse-square-root decay. In a 110M-active, 4.7B-total-parameter MoE over 128B tokens, AIR reaches 1.730 loss versus cosine’s 1.740, with terminal and cumulative, but not peak, learning rate matched.

hot.title: ScheduleGen: Demonstration Generation via Skill Scheduling for Multi-Arm Imitation Learning
hot.summary: ScheduleGen generates multi-arm demonstrations by adapting object-relative contact skills from annotated source demonstrations, planning connecting motions, and scheduling arm paths to respect task order and modeled collisions. Across 28 simulation variants in three frameworks, it averages 79.6% data-generation success and 65.5% policy success. These are equal-weight averages, and policies transfer without real-world fine-tuning, reaching 50% to 80% across eight hardware variants.

hot.title: NyoomFloat12: Accelerating LLM Inference via Lossless 12-Bit Weight Compression
hot.summary: The authors introduce NF12, a lossless format that stores BF16 weights in 12 bits and reconstructs them in a GPU-friendly, fixed-length pattern. It exploits concentrated exponent values and handles rare exceptions separately. On a shared-prefix Qwen3-32B rollout workload, NF12 reaches a peak of 787 output tokens per second versus BF16’s 310, a schedule-dependent 2.54× ratio; gains are not universal.

likes.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False
likes.summary: The authors give a deterministic algorithm for exactly counting satisfying assignments of Boolean formulas with fixed-width clauses. It reorganizes assignment sums into group-by-group sums using shared measurements and interpolation. For each fixed width, the worst-case running time is polynomial in the input size times 2^{O(n log log n/√log n)}, with polynomial space; the exponent improves for linearly many clauses, but this does not give subexponential algorithms for general NP problems.

likes.title: Evolving Agent Teams
likes.summary: Evolving Agent Teams changes how coding agents are organized during GPU kernel optimization. A supervisor diagnoses stalled progress, redesigns roles and coordination, and preserves lessons and code in a shared filesystem. On DeepSeek-V3 MLA paged decode, additional-budget runs achieve 1.21× geometric-mean speedup over production FlashInfer across 47 H100 workloads, with 36 faster; 11 remain slower, without beating the run-stage-only reference.

likes.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
likes.summary: The authors propose a framework for understanding work agents as systems accountable for verified outcomes rather than models producing answers or tool calls. It combines a model, harness, and workspace, and distinguishes persistence—when responsibility can close—from openness—what must be discovered. The survey synthesizes five work forms and capability families but does not establish improved performance or reliability.

likes.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
likes.summary: The authors compare persistent memory systems with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) from raw history, measuring query-level wins and losses against that reference. On LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.6-27B, SimpleMem reaches 73.6% judge accuracy, versus 81.4% for two-round RAG. Results vary across settings, so this comparison does not show that all memory systems underperform.

likes.title: How to Train a One-Step Language Model Without a Teacher
likes.summary: Discrete Beckmann Transport Models (DBTM) learn a time-independent endpoint map from data by minimizing a conservation-equation self-regression objective, with no teacher model or time conditioning. At inference, each map application proposes a complete sequence, and additional function evaluations use commit-and-renoise refinement rather than ODE integration. DBTM reports coherence–diversity Pare

likes.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
likes.summary: FLORE connects force-annotated demonstrations to force-aware control for humanoid contact tasks. Its diffusion policy uses wrist images, robot state, and hand wrenches to predict motion and per-hand force commands, which a controller tracks. On Unitree G1, FLORE succeeds in 24 of 30 rollouts across three tasks, versus 8 of 30 for a position-only policy; evidence is limited to those tasks.

likes.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
likes.summary: ThinkWorld addresses robot-learning by grounding robot actions and annotated human hand motion in a shared discrete Chain-of-Dynamics (CoD) vocabulary. It trains on action-unlabeled videos by rewarding tokens whose predicted futures match observed futures. At deployment, a separate expert predicts continuous actions. In real-robot trials, it achieved 94.4% macro success across six task-condition combinations and succeeded in 52/60 OOD trials.

likes.title: How High Can GPT-6 Astra Climb in Contact-Rich Manipulation? PhysLadder: A Hierarchical, Matched Sim-Real Benchmark for Physical Interaction
likes.summary: PhysLadder evaluates GPT-6 Astra on 16 household tasks in simulation and reality, organized by increasing interaction demands. Each task receives three zero-shot trials per environment, and level means weight tasks equally. Real-world success averages 80.0% at L1, 47.6% at L2, and 0.0% at L3; simulation shows 66.7%, 47.6%, and 0.0%. No L3 task succeeds; results describe this model and setup.

likes.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
likes.summary: EmbeddingGemma 2 maps text, images, audio, and video into an embedding space for retrieval. Modality encoders turn media into tokens that a transformer pools into a vector; modular configurations omit encoders not needed. On MSEB(Retrieval), native audio scores 69.54 MRR@10 versus 57.59 for ASR/text, but uses more parameters. An intermediate MMEB-v2 ablation improves image and video scores, while visual-document performance remains nearly unchanged.

likes.title: Timestral
likes.summary: Timestral is a time-series forecasting model that learns across series and forecasts new ones without retraining. It keeps observed history available while adding separate prediction positions, and assigns covariates roles so known-future inputs can be used without exposing future targets. Timestral-209M ranks first among compared models on six metrics across three benchmarks; this does not isolate DHF’s contribution.

likes.title: Learning Quality-Controllable Robot Policies with Iterative Hindsight Relabeling
likes.summary: QCP lets users request execution quality by labeling successful trajectories with rule-based scores and conditioning a policy on those labels. It collects successful rollouts at the highest label, relabels data by measured quality, and retrains. On a conveyor, its highest-bin policy raises end-effector speed from 188.6 to 257.6 mm/s and throughput from 8.2 to 13.0 cans per minute versus BC.

likes.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
likes.summary: GEPA-Curator improves prompt optimization by selecting task experiences for learning and retrieving a prior success when a task fails. It maintains task histories, skips tasks unlikely to provide useful signal, and gives the optimizer a same-task reference when available. In experiments, it scores 88.6% on GitLab validation; gains vary by setting and do not establish that every failure is noisy.

likes.title: Evolve on Graph: Self-Evolving Knowledge Graph Reasoning without Question Annotations
likes.summary: EoG trains a language model to explore knowledge graphs without annotated question–answer training labels. A Proposer generates graph-grounded questions, executed graph queries supply answer sets, and a Solver’s performance guides difficulty. On five public benchmarks, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct gains 7.46 Hit@1 and 12.05 F1 points over Graph Reranker on average; on IndustryCarBench, it beats ToG by 17.80 Hit@1 points.

likes.title: Native Real-Time Interactive Omni Intelligence: A Unified Framework
likes.summary: The authors present a survey and framework for assistants that understand and respond while inputs and interaction states keep changing, rather than only after a finished prompt. They distinguish broad multimodal ability from using it in ongoing interaction, and describe streaming models and foreground–background coordination. The survey maps evidence but establishes neither a winning architecture nor that interactivity requires capability loss.

likes.title: BEHAVIOR-Spatial Benchmark: Evaluating Spatial Understanding for Robotics
likes.summary: BEHAVIOR-Spatial evaluates spatial question answering, point grounding, and robot action across shared task contexts. Its 3,256 questions cover 49 activities, with 1,240 grounding queries and manipulation and navigation tasks. In a 700-episode simulator prompt probe, oracle dot cues raise soft success from 16.1% to 38.0% and strict success from 10.0% to 24.9%, testing supplied targets, not learned language grounding.

likes.title: NyoomFloat12: Accelerating LLM Inference via Lossless 12-Bit Weight Compression
likes.summary: The authors introduce NF12, a lossless format that stores BF16 weights in 12 bits and reconstructs them in a GPU-friendly, fixed-length pattern. It exploits concentrated exponent values and handles rare exceptions separately. On a shared-prefix Qwen3-32B rollout workload, NF12 reaches a peak of 787 output tokens per second versus BF16’s 310, a schedule-dependent 2.54× ratio; gains are not universal.

likes.title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
likes.summary: StreamVibe pairs a streaming policy that decides when to speak with a Harness tracking active requests, task progress, and prior responses. In full-stream evaluation on Dynamic Intents, adding the Harness to the same StreamVibe-VL (RL) policy raises Content F1 from 5.25 to 8.91 and lowers near-miss FPR from 17.11 to 5.68 at ±2 seconds, supporting improvement in this setting.

likes.title: Know, then Draw: A New Learning Paradigm for Visual Generation
likes.summary: The authors introduce a two-stage text-to-image system: an autoregressive (AR) model predicts visual tokens from a prompt, then diffusion renders pixels from them. They freeze the pretrained AR backbone while training the renderer. A roughly 3-billion-parameter model trained with 6,600 H100 GPU-hours scores 0.86 on GenEval and 87.78 on DPG-Bench, supporting this recipe but not universal superiority or optimal compute allocation.

likes.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
likes.summary: DecisionRAG retrieves evidence by making parallel relevance judgments over candidates in a corpus hierarchy, rather than relying on a conventional first-stage retriever or generating navigation text. Its pretrained, task-untrained Jev model reaches 47.4% R@1 on MultiDoc2Dial and 65.4% Hit@1 on Natural Questions, exceeding dense retrieval plus reranking; results depend on hierarchy, and pruning can hide evidence.

likes.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
likes.summary: GPT-6-Astra directly controls robot manipulation in EBench and can also call post-trained policies to execute motion. The benchmark covers 510 simulated episodes across 26 tasks, using task success and partial stage completion. Direct control reaches 46.7% success; the InternW0-∆ harness reaches 56.0%, above the strongest standalone policy, but high-precision performance remains weak and handoffs can regress.
